title: Evaporator Fan Fault
shortDescription: The freezer evaporator fan is not running at the target speed.
fullDescription:
FE is posted when the BLDC evaporator fan tacho signal is absent. Ice buildup or a failed motor usually cause it.

Defrost manually for 24 hours as a first step; if the error returns after defrost, replace the fan motor.

fixSteps.title: Defrost
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 24 hours with door open.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: If fault returns, fit a new evaporator fan motor.

whenToCallPro: If defrost system damage is also suspected.

faq.a: After a fan replacement, allow 4-6 hours to pull back to temperature.

title: System Communication Error
shortDescription: The user interface cannot communicate with the main control.
fullDescription:
SY (often displayed as SY CE) means the serial link between the display and the main board has dropped. A loose harness after service is the most common cause.

Power cycle, then inspect harnesses if the fault persists.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 5 minutes and restore.

fixSteps.title: Reseat harness
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect and reseat the display-to-main harness.

whenToCallPro: If boards need replacement and you are not confident.

faq.a: Usually yes, it falls back to default settings.

title: Thermistor Open
shortDescription: A temperature sensor reads open circuit.
fullDescription:
OP means one of the thermistors (freezer, evaporator, or fresh food on combo units) reads infinite resistance. The freezer reverts to a default duty cycle until the sensor is replaced.

Inspect the sensor harness first; often OP is a pulled connector, not a failed sensor.

fixSteps.title: Access sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove rear or ceiling freezer panel.

fixSteps.title: Reseat or replace
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat the connector; replace thermistor if resistance is infinite.

whenToCallPro: If the harness is damaged inside the foam.

faq.a: The manual lists which sensor maps to OP; measurement confirms which is at fault.

title: Thermistor Shorted
shortDescription: A temperature sensor reads near zero resistance.
fullDescription:
CL means a thermistor is shorted, which in the control's interpretation is an impossibly high temperature. The freezer then over-runs the compressor.

Replace the affected sensor after confirming with a meter.

fixSteps.title: Measure resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Check thermistor resistance at room temperature.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the faulty thermistor.

whenToCallPro: If harness is not accessible or buried in insulation.

faq.q: Can I swap with any thermistor?
faq.a: No - use the exact replacement part; resistance curves must match.

title: Defrost Heater Fault
shortDescription: The defrost heater did not draw current when energised.
fullDescription:
HD appears when the control energises the defrost heater circuit but the current sensor reports no load. An open heater element, open thermal fuse, or open defrost bimetal are typical causes.

Ice build-up will quickly follow if not addressed, eventually leading to FE and warm storage.

fixSteps.title: Unplug
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect and remove rear freezer panel.

fixSteps.title: Test components
fixSteps.instruction: Measure heater, bimetal, and thermal fuse for continuity.

fixSteps.title: Replace failed part
fixSteps.instruction: Swap whichever component tests open.

whenToCallPro: If you are not comfortable measuring live or near-live circuits.

faq.q: Can I run the freezer until I fix it?
faq.a: Only briefly - ice will choke airflow within a day or two.

title: Ice Maker Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The ice maker temperature sensor or thermistor reads out of range.
fullDescription:
On Kenmore freezers with factory ice makers, IS indicates the mould thermistor or fill sensor has failed. The ice maker is disabled until the sensor is replaced.

Most repairs require replacing the entire ice maker module rather than the bare sensor.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Reset the ice maker using its test button or power cycle the freezer.

fixSteps.title: Replace ice maker
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the ice maker assembly if the sensor is integrated.

whenToCallPro: If water line leaks or fill valve also need service.
videoSearchQuery: Kenmore freezer IS ice maker sensor

faq.q: Will the rest of the freezer still work?
faq.a: Yes, only the ice maker is disabled.

title: Compressor Error
shortDescription: The inverter-driven compressor has reported a fault.
fullDescription:
On linear or inverter compressor freezers, CE is raised when the inverter board cannot start or maintain the compressor. Over-current, locked rotor, and stalled piston are typical causes.

The inverter board is commonly at fault and often cheaper to replace than the compressor itself.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 15 minutes and restore.

fixSteps.title: Replace inverter
fixSteps.instruction: If CE returns, swap the inverter board.

fixSteps.title: Call sealed-system tech
fixSteps.instruction: If compressor itself is bad, sealed-system service is required.

faq.q: Is it worth replacing the compressor?
faq.a: On older models often not; compare cost against a new freezer.

title: Defrost Cycle Timeout
shortDescription: Defrost cycle ran to the time limit without the bimetal opening.
fullDescription:
DF appears when the defrost cycle runs full duration without the bimetal thermostat opening at around 45-55 °F. The thermal fuse usually opens as a safety, killing the heater circuit.

Replace the bimetal (and thermal fuse if open) before returning to service.

fixSteps.title: Unplug
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power and remove rear panel.

fixSteps.title: Replace bimetal
fixSteps.instruction: Fit a new bimetal thermostat on the evaporator.

whenToCallPro: If fault involves the heater or controller.

faq.q: Is it safe to use after DF?
faq.a: Yes, after replacing the bimetal; never bypass the thermal fuse.

title: Condenser Fan Fault
shortDescription: The condenser fan is not spinning at the expected speed.
fullDescription:
CF is the condenser-side fan alert. Dust, a bent blade, or a failing motor block or slow the fan, causing compressor overheating and poor cooling.

Pull the unit out, unplug, and clean or replace the fan as needed.

fixSteps.title: Clean
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum condenser and fan blade.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Fit a new condenser fan motor if needed.

whenToCallPro: If the fault returns even with a working fan.

faq.q: How often should the coil be cleaned?
faq.a: Every 6-12 months, more if pets are in the home.

title: Door Ajar Alarm
shortDescription: The freezer door has been open too long.
fullDescription:
dr (door) displays with a chime when the freezer door has been open more than a preset time, typically 2 minutes. If dr displays with the door closed, the door switch may be stuck or misaligned.

Check the door gasket, alignment, and the magnetic door switch near the top hinge.

fixSteps.title: Close door
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure door closes fully against gasket.

fixSteps.title: Check switch
fixSteps.instruction: Tap door switch - it should click; replace if inoperative.

faq.a: Most models have a mute button that silences the current alarm only.
